title: Nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate near a two-dimensional antiferromagnetic quantum critical point
abstract: We study the effects of zero-point spin fluctuations on the nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate 1/$T_1$ around a two-dimensional antiferromagnetic quantum critical point in the self-consistent renormalization theory. For a weak mode-mode coupling constant $y_1 < $ 0.1, the finite temperature behavior of 1/$T_1$ across the quantum critical point resembles that for only the thermal spin fluctuations. For a strong mode-mode coupling constant $y_1 > $ 0.1, 1/$T_1$ takes its local maximum as a function of temperature in the nearly antiferromagnetic state. Experimental observation of the local maximum in the $^{63}$Cu nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate 1/$T_1$ of lightly-doped superconductors La$_{2-x}$Sr$_x$CuO$_4$ with $x$ = 0.06-0.10 is associated with the effects of the zero-point spin fluctuations. The two-dimensional magnetic quantum critical point and the role of the zero-point spin fluctuations are discussed in the electron spin dynamics of underdoped superconductors La$_{2-x}$Sr$_x$CuO$_4$.
summary: This paper theoretically examines how zero-point spin fluctuations affect the nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate near an antiferromagnetic quantum critical point in cuprate superconductors. Using the SCR theory, the authors show that strong fluctuations predict a characteristic local maximum in $1/T_1$ vs. temperature, which aligns with experimental findings in La2-xSr_xCuO_4.
main_problem: The study investigates the influence of zero-point spin fluctuations on the nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate (1/T_1) near a two-dimensional antiferromagnetic quantum critical point (QCP).
main_result: The theoretical model predicts that for strong mode-mode coupling, 1/T_1 exhibits a local maximum as a function of temperature, a feature experimentally observed in underdoped cuprate superconductors.
method: The authors employ the Self-Consistent Renormalization (SCR) theory, extending it to include zero-point spin fluctuations, and perform numerical solutions for the relaxation rate.
model_or_system: The research focuses on the physics of underdoped superconductors, specifically La2-xSr_xCuO_4, near an antiferromagnetic QCP. The theoretical framework uses the SCR equation to model the spin susceptibility and the resulting nuclear spin relaxation rate.
key_observables: Nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate (1/T_1) as a function of temperature, and the staggered spin susceptibility $\chi^{-1}$.
important_parameters: Mode-mode coupling constant ($y_1$), distance to QCP ($y_0$), and reduced temperature ($t$).
main_assumptions: The theory incorporates zero-point spin fluctuations into the standard SCR framework, and the analysis distinguishes between weak and strong coupling regimes defined by $y_1$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate numerical calculations of the spin susceptibility parameter $y$ and the relaxation rate $1/T_1$ versus reduced temperature $t$ for different coupling strengths, highlighting the temperature-dependent maximum.
paper_structure: The paper develops the SCR theory to account for zero-point fluctuations, analyzes the resulting temperature dependence of $1/T_1$ for weak and strong coupling constants, and compares the resulting theoretical predictions, particularly the local maximum, with experimental data from La2-xSr_xCuO_4.
why_interesting: The connection between zero-point quantum fluctuations, critical points, and measurable transport/relaxation properties in strongly correlated materials is highly relevant to understanding exotic quantum phases.
